Reading now

  • Trustreading · en

    Hernan Diaz, 2022

    An investigation into wealth, power, and who gets to write the official version of reality—told across four competing manuscripts that constantly pull the rug out from under the reader.

    Fiction · Capital & Narrative

  • L'Étranger (The Stranger)reading · fr

    Albert Camus, 1942

    Reading Camus in the original French—deceptively simple sentences where the Algerian sun and quiet existential indifference do all the heavy lifting.

    Philosophy · Absurdism (B1 French)

Finished

  • A Thousand Splendid Sunsfinished · en

    Khaled Hosseini, 2007

    A devastating, deeply human portrait of endurance, unlikely friendship, and quiet defiance across generations in Kabul.

    Historical Fiction

  • Le Petit Princefinished · fr

    Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, 1943

    The rite of passage for anyone learning French, and still sharper about adult absurdity and bureaucracy than most books ten times its length.

    Classic · Fable (FR)

Rabbit holes

  • French, at about B1

    I read French books in the original, slowly, with a dictionary within reach. A few lines I’ve collected are below. See the French log.

  • Two wheels

    A bicycle most of the time, and a motorbike for the longer trips. The 1,500 km Konkan coast ride is on the timeline below. See the route.

  • Photography

    Mostly taken on rides. The photo frames on the Konkan route are waiting for the good ones.

  • The homelab

    The bare-metal box at home that serves this site, and the reason I learn something new about Linux every month. See its readings.

French log

Lines and words I’ve kept from my reading. Open one for the English.

  • « Aujourd’hui, maman est morte. Ou peut-être hier, je ne sais pas. » + −

    Mother died today. Or maybe yesterday, I don’t know.

    Albert Camus, L’Étranger (1942), the opening line

  • éblouir + −

    to dazzle, to blind with light. The sun in L’Étranger does a great deal of it.

    From L’Étranger

  • « On ne voit bien qu’avec le cœur. L’essentiel est invisible pour les yeux. » + −

    One sees clearly only with the heart. What is essential is invisible to the eye.

    Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, Le Petit Prince (1943)

  • les grandes personnes + −

    grown-ups. The Little Prince’s verdict: they never understand anything by themselves.

    From Le Petit Prince

Field threads & milestones

The years so far, in short. Some entries open up: the Konkan coast ride has its route, the Linux switch has a terminal.

2026

  • JulAWS Solutions Architect – Professional

    Cleared SAP-C02, the one I had been circling for a while.

    Three hours, 75 questions, and an unreasonable number of VPC diagrams.

  • Taught a robot to read build logs

    Shipped an agent that watches 30+ pipelines, classifies failures by root cause, and opens the fix as a pull request.

    40% of broken builds now sort themselves out before anyone notices.

2025

  • Halved the AWS bill

    Ran a company-wide cost programme that took monthly spend from $35–38K to $19–21K with no drop in availability.

    Fourteen load balancers became four. Nobody noticed, which was the whole point.

2024

  • DecBecame amber’s DevOps team

    Joined as SDE1 and spent eight months as the only DevOps engineer, owning production for 50+ services.

    One pager rotation, no co-pilot, a lot of respect for good runbooks.

  • Bought my first motorbike, then rode it to all along the coast of Konkan

    Took it down the entire Konkan coast to from Mumbai to Goa and back, a little over 1,500 km of ghat sections, coastal highways, and great food.

    Best infrastructure decision I have ever made without a Terraform plan.

2023

  • OctStarted at IAMOPS

    Consulting across four client accounts on Azure-to-AWS migrations, Terraform, and SRE practice.

  • AugFirst AWS certification

    Earned the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner credential.

    The gateway drug.

  • JunGraduated with a 9.33 CGPA

    Finished a Computer Science degree at Savitribai Phule Pune University with honors in Artificial Intelligence.

2022

  • Switched to Linux full-time

    Made Linux the daily driver and never went back, which is how most of this started.

    Reinstalled exactly once, and that time it was on purpose.

Self-hosted on bare metal in Pune
